# Skarok and A Hard Place

*Pages PDF 3-24*

Orc politics is brutish, nasty, and short. In this scenario, the adventurers are drawn into a schism between two rival Greenskin factions, and are impelled to forge an alliance with one side in order to destroy their stronger enemies. 

Disaster strikes the insignificant and remote settlement of Vergessendorf, when the son of its mayor, Maximillian Schmaling, is seized by some of the Greenskins that infest the surrounding wilds. The kidnappers are a motley band of Orcs and Goblins who follow Skarok Gnawrock, former Orc warlord of the Bonecracker Tribe, ousted by his bitter rival, known as the 'Ard Face. Skarok has too few followers to recover power, but his advisor, a cunning old Goblin called Von Maggot, has concocted a plan. By kidnapping the son of the local human magistrate, he hopes to gain some leverage over whoever they send to rescue him. The rescue party can be pressured into doing Skarok’s dirty work for him — luring the 'Ard Face out from the confines of his encampment and into an ambush, enabling Skarok and his few Boyz to waylay and assassinate him. Skarok can then reclaim his lost leadership with virtually no losses among his own Ladz. 

To secure the life of the mayor’s son, the adventurers must allow themselves to be used as the pawns in Skarok’s plan. Skarok pledges he will release his captive once the 'Ard Face is dead, but can the adventurers trust him to keep his word? Will the adventurers turn the situation to the Empire’s advantage, and slay Skarok once the 'Ard Face is despatched, scattering the Bonecracker Tribe into leaderless, interwarring factions? 

The adventure should take about three sessions — one session to introduce the PCs to the task set by the mayor, and to prepare for that task, which may include the hiring of mercenaries; one session to hunt down Skarok’s lair, be compromised into working for Skarok, and then scout out ways to overcome The 'Ard Face; and a final session to face off against The 'Ard Face, and deal with the aftermath of Skarok returning to power. 

## **Getting Started**
The adventure starts in the remote settlement of Vergessendorf, situated in any area of the Empire surrounded by sprawling, forested wilderness. The adventurers are drawn here for various reasons, for example: 

- They might chance upon the place following a previous adventure in the forest, or during a long journey to elsewhere, glad of the rest they hope its inhabitants offer. 

- They might be directed to the mayor by a mutual acquaintance. This person has pledged to the mayor that he will find suitable individuals to resolve the problem of his missing son — the adventurers are ideal candidates. 

- A faithful servant of the mayor has travelled to the nearest city to seek help. Unfamiliar with citylife, perhaps he falls prey to thugs, and the PCs have an opportunity to rescue him from the criminals. His rescuers prove the perfect recruits for the task at hand. 

Arrival at Vergessendorf takes place at nightfall and the PCs’ first port of call on a cold and wet night should be the town’s only tavern, The Old Crow. Here they will discover that they are not the only strangers in town — a small band of ruffian mercenaries is resting at the tavern, eager for trouble. 

## **Enlistment**
_In this initial part of the adventure, the PCs will spend their first night in Vergessendorf at The Old Crow tavern, and experience a chaotic introduction to the other strangers in town — a band of rowdy mercenaries. The following day, the PCs will be approached by a minion of Mayor Schmaling, inviting them to have an audience with him at his mansion. Schmaling volunteers his chief forester, Emil Hartmann, as their guide into the forest, but before they begin their quest, they might want to bolster their equipment for the job, or increase their fighting strength by hiring the mercenaries they encountered at the tavern._ 

## **The Old Crow**
From the outside, the timber-framed tavern leans at an alarming angle, seemingly ready to topple at any moment. Light streams from the narrow windows, raucous laughter and drunken singing emanate from within — it’s the only lively place in the town. At the door, a young soldier lies face-down, spreadeagled in the mud, an empty tankard in his right fist. Another soldier is on his kness, spitting blood and vomit. Each wears a tabard emblazoned with a snarling boar’s head over their leather armour. 

Inside the tavern, through the fug of pipesmoke, a dozen soldiers, similarly attired, all bearing the emblem of the snarling boar, run riot — swigging frothing brew, dancing on tables, and hurling bottles to shatter against the walls. A gaggle of locals cower behind a table in one corner. The terrified proprietor and his servants hide beneath the bar, allowing the drunken louts to serve themselves beer. A raven-haired man with one eye, evidently the leader judging by the superiority of his arms and armour, stands by the roaring hearth, juggling firebrands. 

The revellers are members of the Wild Tuskers Free Company, a mercenary band recently discharged from the service of a local lord, who have descended on the town while heading east looking for work. Their leader is Vesbastian Kurz, and he and his company might prove useful to the PCs later on. 

The PCs are welcomed as comrades by the drunken soldiers and encouraged to join the revelry. Their only chance of a room at the tavern that night depends on whether they amuse the mercenaries with their antics — the revelry will last into the early hours but food, drink, and a shared room will be granted for free. If they prove to be sober-headed killjoys, Kurz and his men will attempt to turf them out roughly, and if they are ejected their only recourse will be a draughty barn at the edge of town, from which they’ll be kicked out in the morning by an angry townsman. 

## **Vergessendorf**
Vergessendorf is a collection of ramshackle timber houses orbiting a mansion of crumbling brick. At the edge of civilisation, the inhabitants eke a living from the dark forest that surrounds them on three sides, protected from the terrors of the wild only by a high palisade. The skulls of savage beasts and greenskins are staked to the spikes in a pathetic attempt to ward off the danger. The township is entered via a single gate, guarded by crossbowmen in tattered military uniform, wary of strangers. It always seems cold and wet in the village, and the ground underfoot is thick with sucking mud. A damp, musky smell hangs heavy in the air, as does the smoke from the chimney stacks of the town’s decrepit houses, wreathing the atmosphere in a perpetual grey gloom. 

The folk here are pallid, lean, and listless, as though all their energy is sapped by the mere act of day-to-day survival. The only two places of interest are the tavern — The Old Crow — and  the mansion, guarded by fierce spearmen in black coats of chain, and which can only be entered by invitation of the resident mayor. 

The statistics for a typical Vergessendorfer are detailed opposite. 

When a PC interacts with a Vergessendorfer, because of the villagers' aloof nature and distrust of outsiders, any Charm or Gossip Tests count as Hard (–20). However, they are easily cowed, and Intimidate Tests are Easy (+40). 

Due to their abject poverty (Status: Brass 1), Bribery Tests are Very Easy (+60). 

## **Coversations with Commoners**
PCs might learn the following snippets of information over the course of the evening. A PC can do this by interacting socially with the villagers or soldiers, using one of the following Skills: Gossip, Charm, Bribery or Intimidation. Remember to take account of the rules on interacting with Vergessendorfers, given on the opposite page. 

A PC who scores an Astounding Failure for an Intimidation Test against a soldier will be aggressively flung out of the tavern by the aggrieved soldier and his mates, as will anyone else attempting to defend the PC. 

A PC can attempt to eavesdrop on a conversation at a neighbouring table by taking a **Perception** Test ( **Challenging (+0)** due to the hubbub of the tavern). 

A musical PC can try to win over the folk in the tavern using the **Play** Skill. It's a tough crowd, so this is **Challenging (+0)** and any Failure will result in taunts and humiliation. Rewards of Success will occur following the performance. 

Whichever of the above Tests they attempt, for each SL of Success achieved, the PC gleans one of the three pieces of information detailed below. 

A PC can also try to loosen tongues with alcohol, by making an **Opposed Consume Alcohol** Test with a target individual. In this case, each Opposed Test lost by the target results in him or her giving out one piece of information. However, the PC should be careful not to get the target stinking drunk! 

- The forest surrounding the town swarms with Greenskins. When they grow too troublesome, the elector count sends troops to cull them, but this has not happened for several years. 

- If not already aware, the Characters learn that Mayor Schmaling lost his only son in the woods a week back. He went out hunting and never returned. The mayor has sunk into deep depression and neglects his duties. 

- There is talk that the Greenskins are fighting among themselves. This would be an ideal time for the elector count to make war with them, but he has forgotten the people of Vergessendorf, and leaves them to sink into suffering. 

## **Denizens of Vergessendorf**
Vergessendorfers are typical denizens of the Empire in almost every way — poor, fearful of outsiders (but not their coin), and bearing the unshakeable conviction that everywhere outside their village is both wealthier and somehow also worse than Vergessendorf. Most manage to put aside their prejudice where money is concerned, but Characters will otherwise find it difficult to win over any of the obstinate villagers.

## **A Morning Visitor**
The following morning, the PCs are approached by a servant of the mayor, Herr Hoffmann, a haggard, balding man dressed neatly in manservant’s clothes. Their arrival in town has reached the ears of Schmaling. He is eager to recruit them to rescue his son, and has sent Hoffmann to request an audience at his mansion. 

Schmaling is aware of the presence of the mercenaries, but does not trust them to perform the task he requires. He knows that they are likely to demand payment upfront and simply take off with the money, leaving his son to his doom. The PCs, however, are a different prospect. The mayor is an avid reader of Morr’s oracle cards, and a recent reading in regard to the arrival of the adventurers proved extremely positive. He is eager, therefore, to meet them and recruit them to rescue his son. 

## **Audience with the Mayor**
Assuming that the PCs want to meet the mayor (if necessary, Herr Hoffmann has been instructed to promise them whatever enticements are necessary to encourage them to come), Hoffmann ushers them to the mansion to meet Schmaling — see the box below for a description of the mayor and his mansion. 

During the meeting, the PCs will learn the following: 

- A few days ago, the mayor’s son Gaius had been out hunting with Schmaling’s servants, including his chief forester, Emil Hartmann. Gaius hated such sport, but his father believed that such experience was necessary as the mark of a noble gentleman. Schmaling regrets his decision deeply. Gaius, prone to daydreaming at inopportune moments, managed to get himself separated from his guardians. He has not been seen since. 

- Hartmann organised a search which detected Greenskin activity near where Gaius was last seen. 

- Searches have been organised daily since Gaius’s disappearance, but there is no one in Vergessendorf brave enough to venture too far into the forest, and Schmaling is desperate for volunteers with courage and audacity to hunt down his missing son. 

**Skills:** Trade 30 

**Talents:** Beneath Notice, Stone Soup 

**Trappings:** Ragged Clothes (Ugly), Tools of their Trade (Shoddy) 

If Schmaling can get the PCs to volunteer by persuasion alone, all the better, but he can promise any suitable reward, within reason, to entice them to help him. His translation of the oracle cards has indicated (rightly or wrongly) that he can trust the PCs to carry out this task. 

## **Mayor Maximillian Schmaling**
Schmaling is a thin, dour man, sad-eyed with a drooping moustache. As befits his elevated station, he wears a suit of expensive silk and satin, though it is threadbare and patched in places. A tired ruff hangs around his throat. A battered periwig perches on his scalp, grey hairs trailing from beneath it. 

His mansion, in the centre of the town, is an imposing, three-storey brickbuilt pile; impressive at first glance, but at closer inspection the brickwork is cracked, windows are grimed with dirt, and several slate tiles are missing from the roof. Entry is via a series of stone steps leading to the main door, raised above the ground, and guarded by  a couple of diligent spearmen clad in black breastplates and helms. They will only allow entry to strangers with an official invite, or accompanied by one of the mayor’s servants. 

Within, the mansion is dimly-lit, and cluttered with antique furniture. From the wood-panelled walls hang faded paintings and stuffed heads of animals with glassy eyes and patchy, moth-eaten fur. Visitors are met by a decrepit butler, who shuffles them to the mayor’s reception room, where Schmaling sits slumped in a rickety chair, 

half-hidden by a mess of parchment piled high on the oak desk in front of him. 

Schmaling speaks softly, a man of few words, his voice heavy with sadness. Humour is unknown to him. He neglects his work: his sole purpose in life has become the rescue of his beloved son, his only child — Gaius. Schmaling constantly cradles a small gold-framed portrait of his boy. This depicts a young man in his late teens, too sickly-looking to be called handsome, with long, overlycoiffured blond hair, dressed in elegant aristocratic attire.

- A ring fashioned from obsidian. Rubbing the ring, the wearer automatically casts the _Shadowstep_ Lore of Shadows spell on him- or herself, although a roll on the Minor Miscast table is required with each use. This ability can be used once a day, and not in direct sunlight. 

## **Emil Hartmann**
Short, lean, and dark, Hartmann has a beak-like nose and wears green and russet outdoorsman's clothes. He's curt of speech, and difficult to befriend. Armed with a bow and long dagger, he's known the forest paths since he was a child. However, he has a healthy regard for his own safety (some would say he's an abject coward). He'll lead the PCs to the site of Gaius's abduction, and partway into the forest, but he has an uncanny ability to sniff out potential trouble before it happens, and shortly before Skarok's warband launches its ambush, he'll slip away quietly, leaving the PCs in the lurch.

## **Planning Ahead**
The mayor is eager to help the PCs in any way to successfully perform their task. 

- He will send his chief forester, Emil Hartmann, to guide the PCs to the location where his son disappeared, and to accompany them elsewhere, where required. 

- He offers them access to the village store, allowing them to requisition any equipment or provisions they need for the mission. However, such is the state of Vergessendorf's economy that only Common items of poor quality can be gathered. 

- The mayor can open his coffers to allow the PCs to hire the mercenaries in town if they want to boost their fighting strength. Hopefully, the PCs will be on good terms with the Free Company… 

## **Hiring the Wild Tuskers**
If the PCs need a better chance to survive venturing into the forest, they will need back-up. The Wild Tuskers Free Company offers such  reinforcements. The Free Company consists of the wild and charismatic Vesbastian Kurz, the leader, and his unruly band of mercenaries: four swordsmen, four spearmen, and four crossbowmen. They wear black uniforms — the shields of the swordsmen and spearmen are emblazoned with a fierce boar's head design. Profiles for the mercenaries are detailed below. 

Kurz is the man to approach. His price is extortionate — 50 Gold Crowns — but the mayor is willing to empty his treasury if it means the return of his son, either alive or dead, so that the corpse might be given the appropriate rites of Morr. The PCs can try to haggle down the price, and if they manage to do this, Mayor Schmaling will have another reason to be grateful to them. Kurz demands half payment immediately, and the rest on completion of the mission. 

## **Betrayal**
The PCs will need to keep an eye on Kurz — he and his men will attempt to abscond with the downpayment at the first opportunity. The PCs will easily be able to catch up with the band, and must confront Kurz to cow the mercenaries into submission: he will challenge one of the PCs to a duel — should he fall, he and his mercenaries will honour their agreement and follow the PCs into the trees, otherwise they are free of their obligation and can leave with the mayor's money. 

Kurz is a stubborn fighter, and will fight to the death — he will also try to cheat his way to victory. However, if his opponent submits, he will spare their life and claim victory. If anyone other than the duelling PC involves themself in the combat, Kurz's men will act in unison to coerce that PC to cease on pain of death, but will allow the duel to continue. 

The only way to victory for the duelling PC is to kill Kurz. Even at death's door he will try to win. Upon Kurz's demise, there is a tense moment as the distraught mercenaries decide what to do — holding the PCs at swordpoint until consensus is reached. The soldiers decide to honour their late leader's wishes, and lower their weapons, pledging their service to the PCs. Thus honourbound, with oaths to Myrmidia and Verena, they will carry out the mission to the best of their ability. 

If Kurz wins, he and the mercenaries will depart with the downpayment. The only way to retrieve the money in this case is to defeat the mercenaries in combat. 

## **Command & Control**
The PCs are the mercenaries' paymasters, and they will heed the Characters' commands. Commands can be made using Leadership, to impress the men with strength of character, or Intimidate, to cow them into submission. Only one PC at a time can issue an order (though he or she can be assisted as normal). 

Adjust the difficulty of the Test according to how dangerous the order is. A failed order usually means the order is simply not carried out (though see below if the slippery Fuchs is the leader). 

## **Wild Tusker Spearman (4)**
The Wild Tuskers wield the spear in combat far more often than any other weapon. This is both because it is a cheap weapon to provision a solider with, and because the Tuskers have a reputation for standing firm against cavalry charges. Indeed, several of the mercenaries claim that the tusks on the unit's heraldry refer to the many spears they carry into battle.

## **Wild Tusker Swords (4)**
Swords are usually reserved for the best soldiers in a unit, but this is not the case for The Wild Tuskers. The company's reputation as spearmen has led to Kurz being somewhat relaxed about drilling and training with a blade. Still, the company's swordarms are often thrust into combat in towns, villages, or forests, where a long spear might be a hindrance. Casulties in such engagements are inevitably very high, and most Tusker swordarms either quickly seek the right to swap their sword for a spear, drink heavily to drown their worries, or both.

## **Wild Tusker Arbalist (4)**
The Tuskers' arbalists carry heavy crossbows painted to resemble a boar's tusk-filled mouth, dripping with blood. This is done specifically to intimidate their enemies, which works far better when threatening peasants in occupied villages than it does on the battlefield. Still, the mercenaries are decent shots, and the arbalists regularly opine that their bolts spill more enemy blood than sword and spear combined.

## **Promotion**
If Kurz is slain, the PCs will have to choose a new lieutenant to lead the band. Three candidates step forward: Artemius, a burly swordsman, gruff of speech and taciturn; Oder, a lanky spear bearer, heavily scarred, her shield battered, quick of wit and quick to smile; and finally Fuchs, an arbalist, lean and hungry-looking, who talks in whispers. 

A PC might want to make an Intuition Test to evaluate each candidate's demeanour. A separate Test is made for each soldier. Fuchs will try to obfuscate, and so only a Test made against her is Opposed. A PC performing a successful test can glean the following: 

## **Kurz**
Under his leadership, The Wild Tuskers have declined in both moral standing and fortunes. Their former reputation as a reliable mercenary unit is slowly being lost, and the group has fled from at least two major battles during the turmoil in Talabecland. However, word of this has not spread far, and Kurz is inclined to keep ahead of it.

A cautious woman by nature, Oder has a reputation for cowardice that is not quite deserved. The leader acts as a normal allied NPC. Artemius acts belligerently, Oder is brave but cautious, Fuchs thinks only of herself. 

Treat each combatant group as a separate, single entity. Each group acts as one and the members of each group stay together. 

To determine combat results for a group, simply make one Test for the group using a relevant Skill (Opposed by the target if appropriate) — a nearby PC or the mercenary leader can use Leadership or Intimidate to assist that combat, representing them urging their soldiers on with words of encouragement or threats, and can do this as a Free Action. 

## **Fuchs**
In a previous life, Fuchs was an agitator who espoused the need for better working conditions in a mining colony in the Grey Mountains. Wrapped up in a worker revolt that was suppressed by hired swords, Fuchs was surprised to learn that her moral convictions were far more flexible than she had imagined. Fuchs joined up with the Tuskers to avoid the gallows, and has not looked back since.

This Test has the following additional modifiers in close combat: 

- Opponents outnumber the group by 3 to 1: –40 

- Opponents outnumber the group by 2 to 1: –20 

Interpret the overall outcome on that Test, for example: 

- Astounding Success: The group routs their opponents. 

- Impressive Success: The group kills the majority of their opponents. 

- Success: The group kills one of their opponents, without suffering casualties. 

- Marginal Success/Failure: The combat hangs in the balance. Perhaps one of each opposing side is killed or badly wounded. 

- Failure: The enemy kill one of the group, without suffering casualties. 

- Impressive Failure: The enemy kill the majority of the group. 

- Astounding Failure: The enemy rout the group.

## **Into the Forest**
The PCs, hopefully fully equipped and accompanied by a band of loyal mercenaries, now venture into the forest in search of the missing son. Bringing him home, alive or dead, is their task. However, an unexpected turn of events forces the PCs to perform a quest for an unlikely 'ally'. 

At daybreak, the PCs and any accompanying soldiers are guided through the trees by the mayor's chief forester, Emil Hartmann (see page 19 for his stats). 

The path leading to where Gaius was captured wends its way through the dark forest, flanked by impenetrable thornbushes and clinging brambles. The canopy shrouds the forest floor in gloom. The forest is eerily still — no birdsong, not even the croak of a crow — can be heard. 

The scene of Gaius's disappearance still shows signs of a struggle on the forest floor. The ground is churned, and low-hanging branches have been snapped off. A cursory search of the area reveals a bronze buckle, crudely formed into the shape of a leering Greenskin face. An obvious trail leads through the forest eastwards, with drag marks on the ground and foliage hacked away. The prints of large hobnailed boots can be seen in the mud, as well as much smaller footprints — the taloned prints of Goblin feet. 

Hartmann shows the PCs a silver-hilted dagger engraved with the initial G, which he found when he first explored this area. Schmaling, when shown it, confirmed with grief that it belonged to his son. 

A player passing an **Easy (+40) Track** Test can determine that about two or three booted individuals and the same number of Goblins were dragging a human-sized person through the foliage. 

If the PCs blunder along the trail, they will soon fall foul of a Greenskin ambush as detailed below — Skarok has detailed Orcs and Goblins from his band to capture Gaius's would-be rescuers. 

Sensible PCs might be suspicious that it all seems too easy thus far — and indeed they are right. The Greenskins deliberately left clues to their involvement in Gaius's capture, and ensured that the trail is easy to follow, so as to entice the human rescuers into their trap. However, there is little room for the PCs to plan any sort of crafty manoeuvre, for the forest is so dense here that the only way forward is along the trail itself. 

If the PCs decide to backtrack, the wily Skarok has prepared for this eventuality. While the PCs are examining the site of Gaius's capture, a handful of Goblins have snuck behind them to cut off any exit (though Hartmann, wise in woodcraft, can and will evade them). 

Four Goblin spearmen with shields will bar any retreat — screaming shrill battlecries and holding on long enough for their comrades waiting in ambush down the trail to hear them and come running to their aid within a matter of minutes. 

## **The Ambush**
The ambush takes place either further down the trail, or at the point where the four rearguard Goblins hold the line. 

The main ambushing force comprises one Orc and one Goblin per PC and friendly NPC. The Orcs wield brutish cudgels and shields, and the Goblins are each armed with a spear and a net. 

_Entangling_ Quality, and the Goblins The nets have the target opponents with entanglement rather than their weapons. _Entangled_ opponents cannot do anything other than try to break free of the entanglement. 

The Orcs will try to knock out the PCs, preferably when they are entangled. Their clubs have the _Pummel_ Quality. (see page 15 for the stats of the Orcs of the Bonecracker Tribe). 

Remember that Hartmann will sneak off, saving his own skin, at the start of the combat. 

After a few rounds of combat, whenever you feel is most dramatic, the four rearguard Goblins will run into the scene to attack the PCs from behind. 

If the PCs are getting the better of the Greenskins, Skarok himself and the rest of his gang appear from the forest depths. They surround the PCs and Skarok calls a parley. Von Maggot is lurking in the bushes, with a trussed-up Gaius, a blade at his throat. 

If even Skarok is having trouble, Von Maggot steps out with Gaius, and threatens to kill the young nobleman unless the PCs' side lay down their arms. If Von Maggot is forced to slay Gaius, a furious Skarok calls the retreat, taking Gaius's warm corpse with him as an act of petty revenge. 

## **The Bonecracker Tribe**
The Bonecracker Tribe are a band of Orcs steeped in the traditions that have made their kind the bane of the Empire for millennia. They are brutal combatants, occasionally cunning tacticians, and terrifying when gathered in any significant number. The only reason they have yet to conquer the entire Empire is that they enjoy fighting each other more or less as much as they enjoy fighting others. 

## **Greenskins of the Bonecracker Tribe**
The vast majority of the tribe follow the 'Ard Face — as is the custom among Greenskins, they respect the authority of the strongest leader. If the 'Ard Face can be killed, their loyalty will switch back to their old Big Boss, Skarok. They live a nomadic lifestyle, roaming the forest to wherever loot and battle goads them, but are currently holed up in a makeshift camp deep among the trees, where their new leader asserts his authority over them through wanton violence and brutal intimidation. 

## **Skarok’s Band**
The few Orcs and Goblins who have joined Skarok in exile, their loyalty to him is stronger than their fear of the 'Ard Face. They are a tough bunch, but no match for those of the tribe who now follow the usurping Black Orc. They number only about a dozen Orcs and about as many Goblins (fidgety things which are difficult to count), and are far outnumbered by the Boyz loyal to the 'Ard Face.

## **Skarok Gnawrock**
Skarok is the former Big Boss of the Bonecracker Greenskin tribe. His body is a hulking mass of iron sinew, bound in rusting, battle-worn armour. A single massive fang juts from his maw. A single yellow eye gleams evilly from his brutish face. A false eye, carved from rock and crudely painted, is rammed into his left socket. His head is covered with deep scars. A tattoo of the Bonecracker tribal emblem is etched across his chest. His left arm ends in a crude metal claw strapped to the stump. He carries a spiked mace, rows of Greenskin teeth hammered into the wooden haft — trophies of his fallen enemies. 

He is unemotional for an Orc, with an icy demeanour — he tempers his violent instincts, channelling his natural rage only when he needs it. He has a rudimentary cunning, his many years in power teaching him that brains as well as brawn are needed to successfully rule a Greenskin tribe. He certainly has the brawn, but for the brains, he turns to his "trusted" Goblin advisor, Von Maggot. 

Recently ousted by his arch-enemy within the tribe, the Black Orc known only as the 'Ard Face, Skarok spends his time in exile plotting his return to power. 

Skarok plays the role of the adventurers’ ‘employer’, using them to weaken the 'Ard Face, following a plan invented by Von Maggot, so that he can reassume control of the Bonecracker Tribe.

## **Von Maggot**
Goblin advisor to Skarok. Lean and hungry-looking, his deep-set orange eyes gleam with intelligence, uncharacteristic for his species. The Bonecracker tribal symbol is carved onto his forehead. He dresses in a ragged child-sized Imperial greatcoat, black with filth, its tail dragging in the dirt behind him. A heavy metal Imperial skull medal hangs on a chain around his neck — stolen from a captain of the Reiksguard.

Captured during a raid on Imperial territory many years ago, he was kept alive by the unit of Imperial halberdiers that captured him, and used as their lucky mascot — trussed to their standard when they marched into battle. Caged in their barracks for several years before his escape, he learnt much about the ways of men, and acquired knowledge of Reikspiel (hence his appellation ‘Von’). 

Returning to his tribe, he used his knowledge of the Empire to help Skarok in raid after successful raid deep into Imperial territory. Now that Skarok has been ousted by the 'Ard Face, he has come up with a plan to reinstate his Boss, one that involves men of the Empire to do all the dirty work, seeing as Skarok now has so few greenskins under his command. 

He has organised the kidnapping of the son of a local human 'chief', knowing that humans will do anything to protect their offspring, and that the human 'Big Boss' will send competent and hardy mercenaries to rescue the captured boy. Von Maggot plans to ambush the rescuers, and offer them a bargain they will not refuse —  trade the boy in return for the 'Ard Face’s head. With the 'Ard Face dead, the Bonecracker Boyz should typically shift their loyalty back to Skarok. 

## **A Deal with a Green Devil**
This next part assumes the PCs were captured by Skarok in the ambush (see page 19 if the PCs managed to triumph over their attackers). 

The overwhelmed PCs and any accompanying mercenaries will be rendered helpless by his warriors, stripped of any weaponry, and forced to kneel before the huge Orc Boss. 

Skarok does not like to talk much. Von Maggot clambers onto his head and does all the talking in squeaky, broken Reikspiel, with a touch of a Stirland accent, picked up from his time 'serving' with the Third Stirlander Imperial Regiment. 

He  introduces himself to the PCs: "' _Allo, scum! I iz Von Maggot, former mascot o' da Third Stirlanders, now loyal speaker fer me Boss, da great Skarok Gnawrok — 'im bein' Lord of the Bonecracker Tribe, and on whose giant shoulders I iz just now standin._ " 

He then relays the following points to the PCs: 

## **Fightin' for Greenskins?!**
The reaction of the mercenaries to working for an Orc depends on which individual the PCs chose to lead the Free Company. 

## **Artemius**
His hatred of Greenskins means he and his men will desert the PCs as soon as possible. The PCs must use all their powers of persuasion to make him stay — Artemius will be calmed if the PCs mention that they plan to backstab Skarok. The mercenary leader might even come to blows with the PCs over this issue — though a severe beating will cudgel him into submission. If the PCs allow him to lead the mercenaries away, they will be ambushed by Skarok's Greenskins. Despite killing a few of the Orcs, they are overwhelmed. Next time the PCs encounter Skarok's Orcs, they will be carrying the mercenaries' heads as trophies. 

## **Oder**
Ever practical, Oder accepts fate and goes along with the PCs' plans. She just wants to get the job done, get paid, and then get the hell out of this Sigmar-forsaken area. 

## **Fuchs**
Fuchs pretends to go along with the PCs, but secretly hatches her own plan with the Tuskers to betray the PCs once they've rescued Gaius, and capture the young noble herself, ransoming him to his father for a tidy sum. 

- Skarok, through treachery and no fault of his own, has been deposed as leader of his tribe by his bitter rival, the Black Orc known as the 'Ard Face. The Orcs and Goblins present are the only ones who remained loyal to Skarok. 

- Von Maggot has formed a plan to get Skarok back on top where he belongs. In return for the young humie's life, the PCs must get the 'Ard Face away from his main tribe, and into a position where he can be easily killed. 

- With the 'Ard Face dead, Skarok will return as leader of his tribe — all thanks to the wise Von Maggot, his most loyal servant. 

- The PCs can work out how to overcome the 'Ard Face in any way they like. However, Skarok has one demand — he greatly desires to be present at the kill, so he can carve the still-alive 'Ard Face's features from his skull. 

Thus,  Von Maggot insists that the PCs work out how to time their assassination of the 'Ard Face with Skarok's arrival at the scene of battle. If Skarok does not enjoy personally witnessing the downfall of his rival, Gaius will end up as Goblin-fodder. 

- When their task is done, and Skarok is reinstated as Big Boss, he will allow them to leave unharmed with the young humie. If they fail, the humie lad will be eaten. 

During his speech, he is interrupted by a couple of Goblin archers emerging from the forest. One of them carries Hartmann's severed head, a black-fletched arrow piercing his forehead. They cheer excitedly, waving their trophy around. Annoyed at the disturbance, Von Maggot leans over to whisper in Skarok's ear, and the Orc casually stamps on each Goblin, crushing them underfoot. He picks up Hartmann's head and cracks open the skull with his jaw, slurping out the insides and chewing on the cranium, all the while fixing the PCs with an icy stare. 

If any PC tries to interrupt Von Maggot, or if they bravely stand their ground and refuse to work for Greenskins, Skarok impassively swings his axe, cleaving the head off one of the mercenaries, and stares at the PC unblinkingly. Hopefully, the PCs will get the message, otherwise it might take a few more hirelings to slump headless to the ground before they learn to shut up and agree to whatever the Greenskins tell them. 

## **The Map**
Assuming the PCs agree to the deal, Von Maggot slides off Skarok's head, landing deftly before the PCs, whips out a set of crude maps from beneath his coat. These have clearly been created by the goblin, haphazardly scrawled on a handful of torn pages. They show the location of where the 'Ard Face and his warband are currently encamped. 

The PCs can use this map to plan their attack. Apart from the 'Ard Face's camp, there are several locations of potential interest to the PCs, ideal for staging an assassination. These are detailed below. 

## **Reconnaissance**
The PCs have time to scout out two of these places all together, or more if they split up — Von Maggot insists that the 'Ard Face must die before dusk (there are small hunting parties sent out from the Bonecracker camp to track down and kill those who joined Skarok, so time is of the essence). 

Note that any parties of mercenaries sent to scout an area without a PC accompanying them will abscond — stuff that for a game of soldiers! 

Reaching each area requires whoever is out at front to make an **Average (+20) Tracking** or **Outdoor Survival** Test. On any Failure, the PCs blunder into the path of one 

of the scouting parties sent by the 'Ard Face to scour the woods for Skarok and his gang. 

- Marginal Failure: 1d10 Goblins 

- Failure: 1 Orc and 1d10+1 Goblins 

- Impressive Failure: 1d10+1 Orcs and 2d10 Goblins 

- Astounding Failure: 2d10 Orcs and 2d10+2 Goblins 

## **Foiled Ambush**
If the PCs managed to slay Skarok during the ambush, or if he and his Orcs retreated, or if the PCs ran away, there are still opportunities for the party to continue with the adventure. 

If Skarok was forced to murder Gaius and then escaped, the PCs might be tasked by Schmaling to recover his son's body for burial — Schmaling is terrified that the Orcs will eat his son, thus denying his soul passage to Morr's realm. When Skarok (or more likely Von Maggot) realises that he can still use Gaius's corpse as a bargaining chip, he'll try again to force the PCs to take down the 'Ard Face in return for Gaius's body (hopefully not much of him will have been eaten by the time the PCs re-encounter Skarok). 

If the PCs retreated, they can try again to rescue Gaius of course. However, if they somehow extricated the lad from Skarok's grasp in this first encounter, Skarok is in trouble and his followers murder him and join the 'Ard Face — which they also do if Skarok is killed in the ambush. The 'Ard Face, his rank secure, feels confident enough to raid Imperial territory, and initiates a Waaagh!, starting with Vergessendorf. The PCs must lead the mercenaries in defence of the village, and train the villagers to hold the palisades against the relentless Orc attack.

## **' 'Gork S Gap' - the Ravine**
Like a scar carved through the forest, the ravine plunges into seemingly bottomless darkness. About a mile in length, and a thousand feet wide at its widest point, it winds like a snake, its cliffs plunging over 400 feet into gloom. 

On the north-western and eastern edges of the ravine, steep and treacherous natural steps allow those with a head for heights to clamber down to the rocky base far below. 

There are many opportunities for canny PCs to use the treacherous terrain to their advantage if they decide to confront the 'Ard Face here, and these are described as follows. 

## **Steps**
Going up or down the steps requires an **Average (+20) Climb** Test, otherwise a Failing PC will slip and fall. 

## **Fallen Tree**
An ancient oak has toppled across the narrow southern end of the ravine. It stretches 150 feet across the dizzying drop below. Its trunk is ten feet in diameter. An **Easy (+40) Climb** Test is required to span it, otherwise certain death awaits, following a long fall. 

## **Boulder Pile**
On the western side, a pile of large boulders is stacked precariously close to the ravine's edge. Two or more Characters can, with effort (a successful **Assisted Difficult (–10) Strength** Test), dislodge the huge rocks and send them avalanching into the ravine's depths, killing anything standing beneath them. 

## **Jagged Rocks**
On the floor directly below the ravine's eastern cliff, swordsharp, jagged rocks jut like fangs from the surrounding rock. Anyone fighting near here must keep their balance on the uneven ground — a failed **Easy (+40) Agility** Test made at the end of a combat Action means that the character falls, and slices him- or herself on a razor rock, _Penetrating_ and suffering a Damage 1d10+4 hit with the _Impale_ Qualities (the _Impale_ rule takes effect if the Agility Test scores any number divisible by 10 or any double).

## **The Caves**
A spidery network of caves descends beneath the trees. Pitch black and icy cold within, the only sound is the constant splash of water dripping from the stalactites festooning the low ceiling. 

## **Entrance**
Like a yawning maw, the cave entrance is a great black hole in the forest. Anyone taking time to investigate the surroundings of the cave entrance notices that the roof of the cave is crumbling in places — any loud noise, and certainly an explosion, will cause the roof to collapse, injuring anyone standing at the cave mouth, and trapping those within the cave (the fallen rocks can be removed with effort, providing a small gap to allow entry or exit). 

## **Ice Lake**
## **Sinkhole**
Near the centre of the ravine, the ground disappears into an unfathomable sinkhole, its sides smooth and its darkness impenetrable. Anyone pushed into this vanishes for good, their screams taking a full ten minutes to fade into silence. 

A sheet of black ice covers an underground lake, so vast that it disappears into the gloom. A **Challenging (+0) Agility** Test is required to walk on the lake without slipping. An individual who fails the Test not only skids onto their back but risks cracking the ice beneath and sinking into the murky, freezing depths below. 

A Goblin-sized individual will crack the ice on an Astounding Failure, a human-sized character will do so on an Impressive Failure, a character the size of a Black Orc will break through on a Failure, and larger characters on a Marginal Failure. 

_Fatigued_ A character in the icy water suffers the Condition, and remains in this Condition until they get dry. While in the water, their only action is to make a **Hard (–20) Agility** Test to pull themself ashore. If they fail this they must make an **Average (+20) Swim** Test to avoid drowning. 

The eastern edge of the ice lake is solid, rocky ground, which can be traversed safely. 

## **Squig Cave**
A stream of sluggish black water flows from the ice lake north-westwards into a large circular, waterlogged cave. A successful **Hard (–20) Perception** Test allows those who venture into this cave to notice two beady yellow eyes glinting in the darkness, poking from the water. 

The water can be waded into about halfway through the cave, at which point the ground quickly disappears underfoot. In this part of the cave dwells a huge Cave Squig, adapted to live underwater (it has the _Amphibious_ Trait). It attacks anyone entering its lair. 

Clever PCs might find a way of encouraging the Squig to leave its lair, to attack any Greenskins they have lured into the cave… 

## **The Whistling Tunnel**
Turning a corner into this tunnel, the PCs are suddenly aware of an eery whistling echoing towards them. The source of this spinechilling noise is the wind whistling down a narrow shaft  in the centre of a small cave at the end of the tunnel. The shaft disappears up through the roof of the cave, where (by day) a pinprick of light can be seen far above. It vanishes downwards into darkness — dropping a stone down the shaft, there is no sound of it clattering to the bottom. The shaft is unclimbable, up or down. Anyone falling into the shaft will never be seen again. 

The opening of the shaft on the ground can be disguised by a large blanket or other such ruse, or the PCs might try to entice an enemy into the cave and trick them into falling into the shaft. The 'Ard Face is too big to fall into the shaft, but will get stuck up to his midriff if tricked into stepping into it.

## **The Wyvern Trap**
This clearing, 30 feet in diameter, was set up with a trap to capture a rampant Wyvern, on the orders of Skarok when he was leader of the Bonecracker Tribe. Skarok was ultimately laid low by the beast when he was hunting it (the trap never actually worked — the beast simply mauled the Orc half to death in the forest). It was this event hat lead to the tribe's current conflict —— The 'Ard Face took advantage of Skarok's weakened state to usurp him. 

Since the 'Ard Face took over, the Wyvern has roamed free, but recently fell into the trap set for it, its wings ruined preventing it from simply flying out. It struggles in the trap, raked badly by the spiked log, but is still alive — anyone appraoching the trap area will hear its bloodcurdling screams as it tries to wrench itself free from the spikes. The PCs should easily be able to kill it (though will its screams attract Greenskin patrols?). A player who passes an **Easy (+40) Set Trap** Test can reset the trap and perhaps use it to capture the 'Ard Face, using the great beast as bait.

## **Stake**
A tranche of meat is tied to the stake. Either side of the stake is a wide, deep pit, with steep sides and sharpened stakes. When the trap is set, if anything tries to pull the meat from the stake, a spiked log attached by ropes to a nearby tree swings down and hits whoever is at the stake. Make an attack roll to see if the log hits, assuming a Melee Skill of 60. The spiked log counts as causing +11 Damage, and has the _Damaging_ and _Impale_ Traits. 

## **Pits**
The pits are designed to stop the target jumping out of the way of the spiked log. If the target of the trap successfully dodges, they will automatically fall into the pit. Each pit is ten feet deep. The sharpened stakes at the bottom cause anyone falling in an extra 7 Damage, with the _Impale_ Trait (use the result of the Dodge Test to see if the _Impale_ effect is triggered). 

## **Surrounding Forest**
Characters can lie in wait, hiding in the dense undergrowth surrounding the clearing. This is perfect terrain for a party to spring an ambush from.

## **The Mud Pits**
Here we have an area clear of trees, about half a mile across, stinking of sulphur. The land underfoot is heavy with clinging mud, and noxious steam rises from the ground. Here and there, hot water bubbles to the surface, and small geysers hiss and spit boiling liquid. 

## **Bubbling Mud**
Walking in the mud slows down characters — they can only trudge at half pace. They might be caught by the spitting geysers — any character taking a physical action in this area who scores a double on their Test suffers a scald, taking a +8 Damage hit which ignores Armour, but not Toughness Bonus. 

## **Giant Geyser**
Every so often, a huge geyser shoots out from the ground, from the hole in the centre of the area, spraying the place in hot mud as boiling water jets into the air. When the water falls, anyone under the deluge receives a scalding shower. 

At a dramatic point in any encounter taking place here, release the giant geyser. Everyone within 10 feet of the geyser hole is scalded by flying hot mud, taking a Damage +7 hit, ignoring Armour. Everyone rolls a D100, re-rolling ties. Whoever rolls the lowest is struck by the full force of the descending water, and suffers an additional +10 Damage, ignoring Armour. 

## **Goading the 'Ard Face**
Once the PCs have decided where they want to encounter the 'Ard Face, they have to try to work out how to get him there, without also attracting a horde of his minions on his tail. 'Ard Face, as a new leader of his tribe, is determined to prove his strength to the Bonecrackers. He will not, therefore, back down from any challenge. 

The 'Ard Face can be located in his camp, with most of his warriors, numbering a handful of Black Orcs, several dozen Orcs, and many dozen Goblins. A dozen or so of these Greenskins are out and about in the forest, scouring the area for Skarok and his renegade followers. 

The key to luring the 'Ard Face out of his camp are the scouting groups and his obsession to track down and finally destroy Skarok. No doubt the PCs will probably come up with their own scheme to get the 'Ard Face to chase after them, but one sure-fire way is to capture one of the scouts alive, and send them scurrying back to the 'Ard Face with the message that the PCs are working for Skarok, and that they are boasting of helping the Orc chief back to power. 

The 'Ard Face has a bullish personality, trusting in his mighty strength to win the day, and his overconfidence might be his undoing. He believes that the PCs are weak and feeble, and no match for him. This can be used by wily PCs to their advantage. 

## **Skarok Arrives**
At some point, Skarok will want to arrive on the scene to deal the final death blow against his mortal enemy (which disturbingly involves him peeling the 'Ard Face's skin from his skull — not a sight for the faint-hearted). 

This should have been arranged earlier by the PCs as some sort of pre-arranged signal. Whether Skarok arrives too early or too late is up to you — bring him on to inspire the best dramatic effect. He'll have his minions with him, who now hopefully outnumber the 'Ard Face's immediate followers. 

The 'Ard Face will be intent on capturing them and torturing them to learn if their boasts are true, and if so where Skarok can be located. He will emerge to capture them in person — arrogant in the belief that puny humans/elves/dwarfs will soon bow to his will. 

## **The 'Ard Face**
Once Skarok’s trusted second-in-command, the 'Ard Face usurped power over the Bonecracker Tribe while Skarok was recovering from a severe injury sustained while hunting a Wyvern that had invaded his forest territory. Now he is Skarok’s arch-enemy. A massive Black Orc, towering seven feet tall, he is like a wall of muscle encased in crude spiky black armour. 

He carries a huge cleaver engraved with Orcish sigils, and around his neck hangs a necklace of the shrunken heads of his greatest opponents. He is eager to add Skarok’s to the collection. Should the 'Ard Face be killed, it will be easy for Skarok to return to power, but the Black Orc is a formidable foe, and Skarok, exiled with only a handful of loyal Boyz who survived the coup, no longer has the strength to match him in battle. 

## **Fighting the 'Ard Face**
The ultimate battle is the conflict between the 'Ard Face and the PCs. To win this, the PCs will have to have a scheme that is well-planned and well-executed, otherwise they'll risk being overwhelmed by the 'Ard Face's superior numbers. They can use ruses or the terrain to separate the 'Ard Face from the majority of his followers (there will always be a hard core of bodyguards who never leave his side).

## **Aftermath**
If all goes well, and The 'Ard Face dies (and Skarok performed his face-removing ritual on his enemy), Von Maggot and a clutch of Goblins will arrive at the end of the battle, pushing along Gaius, still bound in rope. With a deft flick of his knife, Von Maggot cuts the bindings, and Gaius is allowed to go free, stumbling towards the PCs, pallid with fear. 

Skarok is so pleased with being back in control, he momentairly forgets that he inteded to betray the Characters as soon as they were of no use to him! They may (and should) take this opportunity to leave. If they fail to do so, some of the other Orcs will begin to quite obviously size them up for a fight. If they chose to remain, Skarok will thank them before ordering his Ladz to kill the lot of them — h is in a good mood, after all. 

If the mercenaries are present, they need to such enticement to flee, and will start to back away as soon as it appears possible to escape. 

On the other hand, Skarok will not be pleased if he was deined the opportunity to slice off the 'Ard Face's face, for any reason. Gaius will be sentenced to death unless the Characters intervene. While Skarok is preoccupied with this, the Characters will have a chance to escape, though if they take it Gaius is certain to die. 

## **Victory Feast**
Schmaling will of course be delighted if his son is returned safely. The PCs will receive any reward they were promised, and Schmaling will, reluctantly and shedding a few tears, empty his coffers to pay any surviving mercenaries what they are owed. If the players want to add another PC to their party, one of the mercenaries might decide to step forward with the desire to join their group. 

Schmaling immediately commissions a feast to be held in honour of the return of his son — a desultory meal consisting of watered-down beer, boiled vegetables, and chewy goat meat. 

Gaius proves to be a pompous fool, elevating his own part in events, while denigrating the PCs to maximise his own role in the story. He even manages to mortally insult the leader of the mercenaries, if present, accusing him or her of cowardice in the face of the enemy. 

Whether the PCs decide to pull the enraged mercenaries off Schmaling's son or not is up to them, but Gaius and his father will be mincemeat if nothing is done, and things will escalate, resulting in the burning and looting of the manorhouse and ultimately the entire township. 

By the end of the feast, the PCs will be wondering whether it was all worth it. 

If Skarok dies, whether or not the 'Ard Face perishes too, Von Maggot refuses to release Gaius. If he regards himself in danger, Von Maggot will try to use Gaius as a human shield to escape to safety. Out of vindictiveness, he'll slice Gaius's throat at the first safe opportunity.
